evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.6.1: nīl admīrārī prope rēs est ūna … sōlaque quae possit facere et servāre beātum (Lewis & Short s.v. admīror)

terms.comment: Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
